title: Unit 03: Tenses, Subject-Verb Agreement & Verb Types
subject: english-10

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'By next June, he will have been working in this firm for ten years.'
questions.explanation: 'will have been working' with a time duration ('for ten years') and a future reference point ('by next June') exemplifies the Future Perfect Continuous tense.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'Neither of the boys ___ present in the classroom yesterday.'
questions.explanation: The distributive pronoun 'neither' is singular and takes a singular verb ('was') when referring to past time.

questions.question: Identify the type of verb in: 'The child seems unhappy today.'
questions.explanation: 'Seems' links the subject 'the child' with the subject complement adjective 'unhappy'; therefore, it functions as a linking (copular) verb.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains an INTRANSITIVE verb?

options.A: The author wrote an inspiring story.
options.B: The birds fly high in the sky.
options.D: She baked delicious cookies for us.

questions.explanation: 'Fly' in 'The birds fly high' does not take a direct object ('high in the sky' is an adverbial prepositional modifier), making it intransitive.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'Mathematics ___ considered a foundational discipline for engineers.'
questions.explanation: Nouns denoting academic subjects ending in '-ics' (Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Civics) are plural in form but take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'When I entered the room, the speaker had already delivered his speech.'
questions.explanation: 'entered' is Past Simple, describing the subsequent action, while 'had delivered' is Past Perfect, representing the anterior completed action.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence following the rule of proximity in subject-verb agreement:

options.A: Either the captain or the players are responsible for the victory.
options.B: Either the captain or the players is responsible for the victory.
options.C: Either the players or the captain are responsible for the victory.
options.D: Neither the teacher nor the students was present.

questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'either...or' / 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Players' is plural, so 'are' is correct.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct tense: 'They ___ in this city since 2015.'
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues into the present marked with 'since [year]' requires the Present Perfect Continuous tense ('have been living').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'A pair of shoes ___ kept under the stairs.'
questions.explanation: While 'shoes' is plural, the head noun of the subject phrase is the singular 'A pair', requiring the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Identify the TRANSITIVE verb in the following options:
questions.explanation: 'Polished' transfers action directly to the object 'the table', which makes it a transitive verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Slow and steady ___ the race.'
questions.explanation: When two singular nouns joined by 'and' express a single, compound idea or proverb, they take a singular verb ('wins').

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The jury ___ unanimous in its decision.'
questions.explanation: When a collective noun ('jury') acts as a single, undivided unit (signaled by 'unanimous' and 'its'), it takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The jury ___ divided in their opinions.'
questions.explanation: When members of a collective noun act individually in disagreement (indicated by 'divided' and 'their'), it takes a plural verb ('were').

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'I will be preparing for my final examinations this time next week.'
questions.explanation: 'will be preparing' represents an ongoing action at a specific time in the future, which is the Future Continuous tense.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'Each of the participants ___ awarded a certificate.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is an indefinite distributive pronoun that strictly takes a singular verb ('was awarded').

questions.question: Select the correct sentence with proper subject-verb agreement:

options.A: The quality of these mangoes is exceptional.
options.B: The quality of these mangoes are exceptional.
options.C: The quality of these mangoes were exceptional.
options.D: The quality of these mangoes have been exceptional.

questions.explanation: The subject is the singular head noun 'The quality' (not the plural modifier 'mangoes'), so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'She had been writing letters before the power went out.'
questions.explanation: 'had been writing' indicates an action that was ongoing in the past up until another past event ('the power went out'), defining the Past Perfect Continuous tense.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'Bread and butter ___ his favorite breakfast.'
questions.explanation: 'Bread and butter' denotes a single collective dish / unified concept, thus taking the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Ten kilometers ___ a long distance to walk.'
questions.explanation: Quantities of distance, time, weight, or money are regarded as a single total quantity and take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Identify the function of the underlined verb: 'He *grew* tired after the marathon.'
questions.explanation: 'Grew' does not denote agricultural cultivation here; it describes a transition of state and connects the subject 'He' with the adjective predicate 'tired', functioning as a linking verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'The Prime Minister, along with his ministers, ___ arrived at the venue.'
questions.explanation: Parenthetical phrases introduced by 'along with', 'as well as', 'together with', or 'in addition to' do not affect the grammatical number of the subject ('The Prime Minister' is singular -> 'has arrived').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'None of the leaked information ___ authentic.'
questions.explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun. When 'none' refers to an uncountable noun, it requires a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'I have finished my breakfast.'
questions.explanation: 'have finished' is composed of auxiliary 'have' + past participle V3, representing the Present Perfect tense.

questions.question: Which of the following verbs is an IRREGULAR verb in English?
questions.explanation: 'Catch' forms its past tense and past participle irregularly as 'caught, caught' (without the standard '-ed' inflection).

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Every man, woman, and child in the village ___ rescued.'
questions.explanation: When subjects preceded by 'every' or 'each' are joined by 'and', the verb remains singular ('was rescued').

questions.question: Select the correct form: 'Fifty thousand rupees ___ a fair price for this laptop.'
questions.explanation: A specific sum of money considered as a unit takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Identify the tense of: 'The train had left before we reached the station.'

options.A: Past Perfect in the main clause, Past Simple in the subordinate clause
options.B: Past Simple in the main clause, Past Perfect in the subordinate clause

questions.explanation: 'had left' is Past Perfect (the earlier event) and 'reached' is Past Simple (the later event in past time).

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'More than one candidate ___ qualified for the interview.'
questions.explanation: Under standard formal grammar, the expression 'more than one' followed by a singular noun takes a singular verb ('has qualified').

questions.question: Identify the type of verb: 'He gave me a precious watch.' The verb 'gave' is:
questions.explanation: 'Gave' takes two objects: an indirect object ('me') and a direct object ('a precious watch'), making it a ditransitive verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither you nor I ___ invited to the ceremony.'
questions.explanation: By the rule of proximity with 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the pronoun closest to it ('I' -> 'am').

questions.question: Identify the sentence written in the PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS tense:

options.A: It has been raining continuously since dawn.
options.B: It was raining continuously when I awoke.
options.C: It is raining continuously right now.
options.D: It will have rained by tomorrow.

questions.explanation: 'has been raining' combines 'has been' with present participle '-ing', indicating Present Perfect Continuous.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The committee ___ divided on this controversial issue.'
questions.explanation: When members of a committee are in disagreement, the collective noun functions plurally ('are divided').

questions.question: Identify the regular verb among the following:
questions.explanation: 'Construct' forms its past tense and past participle regularly by adding '-ed' ('constructed, constructed').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'The scissors ___ on the cutting board.'
questions.explanation: Tools and garments consisting of two matching parts (scissors, trousers, binoculars, forceps) are grammatically plural and take plural verbs ('are').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'If he ___ harder, he would have secured the scholarship.'
questions.explanation: In Third Conditional sentences, the if-clause takes the Past Perfect tense ('had worked') to match 'would have + V3' in the main clause.
